description: fylite — a self-contained tokamak equilibrium / transport / turbulence kernel. One command family on three hosts: the Python console script (this spec built into argparse), the ONE Rust executable fylite (the same spec built into its parser; carries app / data / case natively) and the browser app (its launch parameters are the `hosts.app.params` below). Commands list the hosts that carry them; a host that does not carry a command delegates it (Python -> the bundled Rust executable, command word first) or refuses it by name.

python.note: argparse parser built from this file (engine/cli.py). Carries every command; `app`, `data` and `case` are delegated verbatim to the one bundled Rust executable under fylite/_bin/ (or --bin-dir), with the command word put back in front.

rust.note: THE executable — one, since 2026-09-03. The whole app/ is embedded and every command word is carried here: `app`, `data`, `case`. With no subcommand it runs `app` (serve the UI on loopback and open the browser) so a double-click still works. The thin fylite-data / fylite-case alias binaries were retired into this one; whoever needs `data` supplies the word (`fylite data ...`, or `fylite data ...` through the Python host).

app.note: The browser app takes its launch parameters from the URL. They are defined here once; `fylite app --<name>` writes them into the URL it opens, and a gate asserts the pages read exactly these names.

machine-readable output
print the case -> entry mapping and the full field accounting (mapped / sub-capability / shared / ui), without running
